**[2026] VJS 13 — appeal panel, pragmatist opinion.** Disposition: allow in part — (a) varied; (b) and (c) stand.

Ask what each rule produces. A business whose policy authors do not use git does not stop editing policy under (a): it edits elsewhere, and the repository files become a fiction the gate validates cleanly. A rule people route around yields a record that lies — worse than no rule.

The challenge's route has its own bill. A digest verifies a document you can already fetch; it does not retrieve one. If the external store overwrites versions, VJS 11's version-in-force citation fails six weeks later, and the gate loses its named denial.

So vary (a): stage the cheap thing — the adopted version's name, digest and date. Prose lives where authors reach it; adoption becomes a release step, borne by whoever already ships the enforcing code. Divergence then shows as a mismatch. Prefer loud failures.

*(150 words, r.14.)*
